# git: fetch tags from different pull call

Stop `pull` from replacing local tags when it fetches from another remote. The whole note is "it replaces current tags": with several remotes (`origin`, `upstream`, `mirror`) a tag that exists under the same name at two of them, or only at one of them, is overwritten or dropped by a fetch that treats every remote as authoritative for tags.

At the time `git-pull` ran `git fetch --all --prune --prune-tags --tags` before the pull — the form still visible in the 2022 snapshot: `--prune-tags` deletes every local tag absent from the remote being fetched, and forced `--tags` overwrites clashing ones. Expected: pulling from any remote leaves the tags of the other remotes intact; only tags the remote actually owns are updated, and nothing is deleted silently.
